subject: midwife toad
title: This Toad Dad Wraps 80 Eggs Around His Legs and Carries Them for Weeks

scenes.text: This male toad carries the eggs. Wrapped around his legs.
The common midwife toad of western Europe. After mating, the male winds strings of 20 to 80 eggs round his hind legs.
He carries them for four to seven weeks, keeping them moist.
Some males take clutches from two, three or four females, and carry more than 150 eggs.
When they're ready to hatch, he wades into a pond and the tadpoles swim off his legs.
So who carries the kids? Dad. Up to 150 eggs on his legs.

description:
The male common midwife toad carries strings of 20 to 80 eggs wrapped around his hind legs for four to seven weeks.
Found across western Europe, the male winds the eggs around his legs after mating and keeps them moist until they are ready to hatch, then carries them to water where the tadpoles are released. Some males take on the clutches of two to four females and carry more than 150 eggs at once.
Which animal has the most devoted father?
first_comment: Its cousin on Majorca was described from fossils in 1977, then found alive in 1979. Which animal dad deserves the most credit?
